facts: On 23 August 1939 Germany's foreign minister Ribbentrop flew to Moscow and Stalin shook his hand. That night Molotov and Ribbentrop signed a non-aggression pact. A secret protocol divided Poland and the Baltic states between Germany and the Soviet Union. Nine days later, on 1 September, Germany invaded Poland; on 17 September the Red Army invaded from the east. On 22 September German and Soviet troops held a joint parade in Brest. In June 1941, less than two years later, Hitler broke the pact and invaded the Soviet Union.

lines.say: On August 23rd, 1939, Nazi Germany's foreign minister flew to Moscow. Stalin shook his hand.
That night, Molotov and Ribbentrop signed a non-aggression pact, with Stalin looking on.
A secret protocol split Poland and the Baltic states between them.
Nine days later, Germany invaded Poland. On September 17th, the Red Army invaded from the east.
Five days after that, German and Soviet troops held a joint parade in Brest.
Less than two years later, Hitler broke it and invaded the Soviet Union.
